references.text: The Sabbath burnt offering is mentioned as a fixed weekly offering in addition to the daily offerings, showing that the Sabbath had its own obligations beyond the festivals.
This verse distinguishes between the appointed festival offerings and voluntary gifts and vows, just as Leviticus 23:38 does.
Refers to voluntary offerings (נְדָבָה) as a category of offering that Israel could give in addition to the required offerings.
Lists various types of offerings including vow offerings (נֶדֶר) and voluntary gifts (נִדְבָה), the same categories mentioned in Leviticus 23:38.
Distinguishes between tithes, vow offerings, and voluntary gifts that were to be brought to the sanctuary.
Mentions both vows (נֶדֶר) and voluntary offerings (נְדָבָה) as reasons for bringing offerings to the Lord.
Describes voluntary gifts (נְדָבָה) that the Israelites brought for the work of the Lord, reflecting the same principle of voluntary service through giving.
